# R98 prospective action-aligned acquisition protocol

## Identity and nonreplacement

This protocol is deposited before R98 acquisition, validation, or test execution. The baseline is the R97 manuscript at f802fe64d91d9f5c1c8f86123b0fbe114e622279 and its review at 9723c6cd2cc8b3e071422f3e522d4a843946db63. R96 and R97 findings remain separately identified and unchanged. In particular, R97 reduced all 36 spans while total first-proposal rejections rose from 644 to 757, quadratic least squares was the observed winner, and no R97 adoption cell certified adoption over quadratic least squares. This experiment does not relabel those findings.

## Primary experiment

The economic primitives, two-date recursive AVaR service, risk levels 1/2 and 3/4, original continuous innovation law, terminal controller, feasible action rounding, original-optimum tolerance 1/256 and policy-cost width 1/8192 remain unchanged. The three families are quadratic, oblique ReLU, and coordinate spline. Each has design rank six and three nonlinear features, selected from its original 32-feature dictionary. All families receive the same 1,024 training sites and original-model value/support information at each risk level. A support slope is not mislabeled an exact derivative of the optimal continuation.

Training sites are successor states of prespecified primitive draws: a uniform 20-bit dyadic initial state, a uniform feasible investment fraction, and a uniform dyadic innovation fraction. PCG64 SeedSequence [2026101498, 1, risk-index] fixes these construction draws. The executed floating-point successor coordinates are retained as exact binary input data. This acquisition design targets the reachable continuation domain; it is a new matched acquisition, not an unchanged R97 fit.

Within each family, value least squares first selects three features with the R97 rank checks, nonnegative nonlinear coefficients, 1e-12 numerical tie rule and 30-bit dyadic readout rounding. The frozen seven-candidate menu is: (0) value least squares; (1) interval-span readout, retained only if the same 32-by-32 whole-domain validator does not worsen its span; (2) the rounded half mixture of 0 and 1; and (3)-(6) constrained least squares with value loss plus directional-support loss weighted by 1/64, 1/16, 1/4 and 1. The directional design is the derivative of the acquired features in the original investment exposure direction (1/2,1/4). Intercepts and affine coefficients remain free; nonlinear coefficients remain nonnegative. The candidate menu is not expanded after validation. Solver failure aborts the campaign and is retained; it is not silently dropped.

Every candidate is rounded, serialized, reloaded and whole-domain checked. Label generation, all feature trials, readout solves, rejected readouts, all domain checks and every validation service are charged. Shared or inherited information is identified; it is not an uncharged oracle. The full-selector acquisition cost is distinct from the cheaper standalone least-squares acquisition.

## Selection and prospective test

At each risk level, 128 fresh uniform 20-bit dyadic initial states are drawn from operating-system random bytes, stored before use and shared across all families/candidates. The selector minimizes first-proposal rejection count under the unchanged original-model qualification rule. Ties are broken by total terminal proposal queries, then by the sum of all recorded operation-event counters, then by candidate index. Operation-event counts are not called floating-point operation counts. Every candidate runs the complete service, including paid repair, refinement and exact fallback; no row is discarded. This is a rejection-aligned loss with complete-work validation, not a guaranteed wall-clock optimum.

After all six choices are made, a selected-model manifest, executable payloads, validation hashes and source hashes are written and committed to the remote research branch. Only then are 1,024 new initial states per risk level drawn and stored. These independent test states evaluate each of the six selected services, its newly acquired value-LS control, the unchanged R97 rank-six/1,024-label quadratic-LS service, and the online service. Identical frozen payloads may share a recorded deterministic replay, but such reuse is explicit; no repeated replay is counted as a new observation.

The prespecified 16 paired nested-policy-cost contrasts are: selected versus own value-LS (six); selected nonquadratic versus frozen R97 quadratic-LS (four); and selected versus online (six). Each row difference is intersected with the deterministic interval [-1/256,1/256]. Outward sample-mean intervals are enlarged by (1/256)*sqrt(2*log(32/0.05)/1024), giving a familywise Hoeffding confidence account conditional on all pre-test acquisition and selection. No R96 interval is transferred to a refit. Exact identity of complete services implies zero contrast and is reported as identity, not improvement. Six paired selected-versus-own-LS rejection differences use their own 95-percent familywise Hoeffding account on [-1,1].

The primary economic target remains nested original-law policy cost, averaged over the stated initial-state law; this is not a new empirical welfare calibration. The engineering equivalence margin remains 1/1280 and is not reinterpreted as a calibrated welfare margin. The confidence theorem assumes the stipulated independent random draws; recorded bytes and state files permit deterministic reproduction.

## Work, timing and independent checks

Seven sequential fresh-process timing repetitions use 32 independent prespecified timing states at each risk level for the six selected services, two frozen R97 quadratic-LS services and two online services. Report all repetitions, medians and ranges; clocks are descriptive on the recorded host, not confidence bounds for another host. Preserve all raw counters, acquisition costs, first-proposal losses and widths, rejections, repair, refinement, fallback, memory and serialization evidence. There is no energy claim.

The fitting audit separately assembles feature matrices, reproduces bounded least squares by enumerating active sets rather than calling the production fitting routine, checks selection and coefficient rounding, and reconstructs serialized functions. Interval-span optimality and whole-domain validation receive separately stated numerical/exact checks; a shared numerical kernel is disclosed rather than called algorithmically independent. Arithmetic mechanism tests cover action-support bounds, risk-tail transfer, nonuniform-law information constants, randomized sound-interval quantifiers, posted-price decision loss and work-margin integrability.

Broader horizon, multidimensional-control and calibrated-application claims require separately executed evidence. The present experiment does not fabricate those observations. A publication includes a claim-to-evidence map and a content-retention map, while keeping Neural Bellman Operators as the original paper's subject.
